content.user_title: Analyze Startup Metrics and Unit Economics
content.value_statement: Startup teams need clear metrics to judge growth, retention, and cash efficiency. This skill maps formulas, benchmarks, and reporting guidance to each startup model and stage.
actual_capabilities: Explains core formulas for MRR, ARR, CAC, LTV, payback, burn multiple, NDR, and Rule of 40.
Maps metric priorities to pre-seed, seed, Series A, and later startup stages.
Covers SaaS, marketplace, consumer, mobile, and B2B sales metrics.
Provides benchmark ranges for growth, retention, sales efficiency, liquidity, and runway.
Guides board, investor, and operating dashboard metric presentation.
Highlights common tracking mistakes such as vanity metrics and weak segmentation.
limitations: Does not connect to analytics, billing, CRM, or finance systems.
Benchmarks are general ranges and may not match every market or company model.
Does not verify user-provided metric data for accounting accuracy.
Does not provide legal, tax, investment, or fundraising advice.

use_cases.title: Define Seed Metrics
use_cases.description: Choose the five to seven metrics that best show growth, retention, unit economics, and runway before a seed raise.

use_cases.title: Improve SaaS Efficiency
use_cases.description: Review CAC, LTV, payback, NDR, magic number, and burn multiple before increasing sales and marketing spend.

use_cases.title: Prepare Investor Reporting
use_cases.description: Create a concise investor metric snapshot with current values, trends, benchmarks, and operational interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Core Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: My startup is [stage] and uses a [business model]. Recommend five core metrics to track weekly and explain why each matters.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Unit Economics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these values to calculate CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, and payback. Values: [paste data]. Explain what the results mean.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Growth Efficiency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these startup metrics: [paste metrics]. Identify the strongest signals, weak signals, and three actions for the next quarter.

prompt_templates.title: Build Investor Narrative
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Series A investor metrics narrative from these metrics: [paste data]. Include benchmarks, risks, and questions investors may ask.

output_examples.input: Seed B2B SaaS company with $80,000 MRR, 14 percent monthly growth, CAC of $1,500, and 14-month payback.
output: Track MRR growth, CAC payback, gross retention, burn multiple, runway, and pipeline coverage.
The payback period is acceptable for seed stage. Validate retention before increasing sales spend.

output_examples.input: Marketplace team wants to know whether supply and demand are balanced.
output: Review GMV growth, take rate, fill rate, time to transaction, repeat rate, and supply-demand ratio.
Low fill rate with growing demand suggests a supply constraint. Low repeat rate suggests weak customer value.

output_examples.input: Founder preparing a monthly investor update after reaching $3 million ARR.
output: Show ARR, monthly growth, NDR, CAC, LTV:CAC, burn, runway, and burn multiple with trend context.
Add one short explanation for each metric that is below the relevant benchmark.

best_practices: Track a small set of core metrics consistently before adding secondary dashboard views.
Segment metrics by customer type, channel, cohort, and product line when decisions depend on those differences.
Pair every metric with a benchmark, trend direction, and clear operating action.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize vanity metrics such as total users without retention or activation context.
Do not compare metrics across business models without adjusting formulas and benchmarks.
Do not scale sales and marketing spend before CAC payback, retention, and runway are understood.

faq.question: Which startup stages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers pre-seed, seed, Series A, and later stages with different metric priorities for each stage.

faq.question: Can it calculate CAC and LTV?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the formulas and can calculate results when you provide the required inputs.

faq.question: Does it support marketplace metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers GMV, take rate, fill rate, repeat rate, liquidity, and supply-demand balance.

faq.question: Can it build a dashboard automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides metric selection and structure, but it does not connect to dashboard tools.

faq.question: Are the benchmarks exact targets?
faq.answer: No. They are general ranges that should be adjusted for market, pricing model, and company stage.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It is an educational framework and should be reviewed with finance, legal, or investment professionals when needed.
